rules.notes: Dead store persistence lowered from 70% to 55% after May backtesting. Rate-based decline scoring confirmed better than volume-based.
lessons_learned: SEASONAL_RECOVERY (May 2026): Dead store persistence prior must drop to ~35-40% in May-Jun. Kharif demand reactivates dormant stores. Filed 2026-05-31.

predictions.prediction: 100 dead April stores → 70%+ will remain dead in May
predictions.evidence: April had 100/144 dead stores. Historical pattern: once dead, stores rarely self-recover without intervention.
predictions.actual: Only 54.2% stayed dead. 66 stores (46%) came back in May.

diagnosis.evidence: Filed during Apr (pre-Kharif trough). Scored in May when Kharif season prep began. Demand pulled dormant stores back to life — not an intervention, pure seasonal reactivation.
diagnosis.lesson: Dead store persistence prior must be reduced to ~35-40% in May-Jun (Kharif season). Stores that look dead in Feb-Apr often reactivate when Kharif demand arrives. Current prior of 55% still too high for this period.

predictions.prediction: Top 50 declining stores → 40%+ will go completely dead in May
predictions.evidence: Top 50 stores by volume showing >10% decline from March to April. High volume + decline = at risk.
predictions.actual: 0% of top 50 declining stores went dead. All 50 continued to fulfill.

diagnosis.evidence: Priority score used Apr_orders × 2 (volume-based). This selected the LARGEST declining stores. Large stores have inertia — they rarely die in a single month even with a 20-30% decline. The stores that actually die are SMALL stores with STEEP decline rates, not large stores with gradual ones.
diagnosis.lesson: CRITICAL: Never rank declining stores by volume. Rank by decline RATE. A store dropping from 10→2 orders (80% drop) is 10x more at risk than a store dropping from 100→80 (20% drop). Formula: priority_score = prev_orders × decline_rate × urgency where decline_rate = 1 - (current/prev).

predictions.prediction: LMD hold problem will persist in May — majority of 333 stores still >40% HOLD
predictions.evidence: 333 stores (33% of network) had HOLD_BY_LMD > 40% in April. This is structural LMD behavior, not random.
predictions.actual: 68.5% of those 333 stores still had HOLD_BY_LMD > 40% in May. Problem persisted without intervention.

candidate_rules.description: Dead store persistence prior is too high in May-June (Kharif season). 46% of April dead stores reactivated in May — nearly double the 25% we assumed.
candidate_rules.evidence: 1 of 1 SEASONAL_RECOVERY diagnoses shows this pattern (100%). Small sample but high confidence due to known agricultural cycle.
candidate_rules.suggested_rule: Reduce dead_persistence_prior from 0.55 to 0.35 during May-June. Restore to 0.55 in July onwards.

candidate_rules.description: Volume-based decline scoring selects wrong stores. Large stores with moderate declines never die. Small stores with steep declines always die.
candidate_rules.evidence: PRED-002 was 100% wrong. Top 50 by volume = 0% mortality. The correct signal is decline RATE, not volume.
candidate_rules.suggested_rule: Replace priority_score = apr_orders × 2 with priority_score = prev_orders × (1 - curr/prev) × urgency. Apply immediately.
